events.text: A note slides under your door, written in the Under-Cloud's cipher: a job for a new face in the Under-Cloud Market, small lifts at the Isle Bazaar, half the take in advance.

ok.log: It goes cleanly. The second half arrives the next morning.

fail.log: It goes wrong, and the wardens learn a little more about you.

effects.log: You take the advance and vanish for a season. The Under-Cloud remembers.
You burn it. You sleep well, for once.

events.text: A junior warden of the Jade Court stops you on a bridge of the Isle Bazaar, looks at your hands for a long time, and says nothing.

effects.log: You say nothing. They walk on. You do not breathe until they are gone.

choices.text: Offer them a stone for their trouble

effects.log: They take it. You are not sure what you bought.

ok.log: They say only "careful." You are, for a while.

events.text: A fence who pays in chipped stones looks over what you brought and offers half what it is worth, because they know you cannot go anywhere else.

effects.log: You take it. Stones are stones.

ok.log: You get three quarters. They respect you more.

effects.log: You keep them. They are hot, and so are you.

events.text: Another thief of the Upper Realm, younger and bolder, wants to work with a new face in the Under-Cloud Market: two pairs of hands, half the risk.

effects.log: You work together all season. It is easier and less private.
You refuse. They go off alone and are caught within a year.
You teach them enough not to be caught. They owe you.

events.text: You learn that the stones you lifted last month belonged to an immortal saving for their child's first tribulation pills.

effects.log: You give them back. The immortal tells the wardens a miracle happened.
You keep them. You think about it more than you meant to.

choices.text: Steal the pills and leave them instead

ok.log: You leave the pills on their doorstep. Nobody understands.

fail.log: You are nearly caught being kind.

events.text: An old thief of the Under-Cloud Market tells you the rules above the clouds: never from a minister's child, never from the poor isles, never a second time from the same house.

effects.log: You swear. The old thief nods and introduces you to better fences.
You laugh. The old thief stops talking to you.
They tell you stories for a whole night.

events.text: The wine houses are telling stories about a new thief nobody can name yet. Most of them are wrong. Some of them are flattering.

effects.log: You listen. The stories are better than your life.
You send a note to a teller. The story improves.

choices.text: Leave the isle for a while

effects.log: You leave. The stories go on without you.

events.text: The job is too easy: a treasury with its ward open, a warden asleep, a chest unlocked.

effects.log: You walk away. Next morning the wardens are seen leaving the treasury, disappointed.

ok.log: You take one thing and are gone before the trap closes.

fail.log: The trap closes on your sleeve.

events.text: A letter climbs the white stairs: someone from your old life below has heard you are a great immortal now, and is proud.

choices.text: Write back about your honest work

effects.log: You write about the work you pretend to do.
You tell them. They write back that they always knew you would be interesting.

choices.text: Send them a gift of stones

effects.log: You send stones down. They will never know where from.

events.text: Someone has been doing jobs on your isles and signing them with your mark, badly.

ok.log: You find a young thief who admires you. You teach them a better mark.

fail.log: You cannot find them. The wardens think it is you.

choices.text: Do a perfect job and sign it

effects.log: You do one perfectly. Everyone can tell the difference now.
You let them. The wardens catch them, not you.

events.text: One evening above the clouds you realise you have enough stones, enough stories and enough scars, and that you could stop.

effects.log: You stop. Your hands itch for a century, then stop itching.
You say one more job. Everyone says that.
You laugh. Stopping is for other people.

events.text: A poor isle's elder asks a new face in the Under-Cloud Market to steal back their isle's water-seal from the faction that took it by a crooked law.

ok.log: The seal goes home. The isle never says your name, and lights a lamp for you.

fail.log: The faction catches you at the edge of the isle.

effects.log: You refuse. The elder understands, and is sad.

choices.text: Take it to the Jade Court instead

effects.log: The Court rules against the faction, slowly.

events.text: A skiff captain offers to carry unstamped stones past the Court's tollhouses for a new face in the Under-Cloud Market, for a share.

effects.log: The stones go through. The captain wants more next time.

ok.log: You fly them past at night.

effects.log: You decline. The captain finds someone else.

events.text: A child of the isles follows you through the bazaar, watching your hands with great admiration. They want to learn.

effects.log: You teach them to work a stall. They never know what you were.
You teach them. They are better than you in a decade.
You send them home with a stone. They keep following you anyway.

events.text: A thief you know has been taken to the Cloudless Cells, and their family on the isles has nothing.

effects.log: You send them stones every season.

ok.log: You get them out on a night with no wind.

effects.log: You stay away. It is safer.

events.text: The Under-Cloud's old lord asks a new face in the Under-Cloud Market to lift a relic from a faction's vault: an immortal's first sword from below, worth nothing up here and everything to its owner.

ok.log: You take it. The faction lord is beside themselves.

choices.text: Take it and give it back to its owner

effects.log: You find whose it was. They weep.
You decline. The old lord is surprised, and amused.

events.text: A junior warden of the Jade Court offers a new face in the Under-Cloud Market a deal: work for the Jade Court, catching other thieves, and the past is forgotten.

effects.log: You accept. You are very good at catching thieves.
You refuse. The offer will not come twice.
You accept and warn everyone you catch.

events.text: A quiet year above the clouds. No jobs, no wardens, nobody looking. The Under-Cloud Market forgets your face a little.

effects.log: You enjoy it. The notice fades.
You plan. It will be the job of the age.

events.text: A treasury pavilion's ward is a puzzle older than the Jade Court: nine locks of light, and a wrong guess wakes every warden on the isle. A fence who pays in chipped stones says a new face in the Under-Cloud Market is the only one who could.

ok.log: The ninth lock opens. You take only what you came for.

effects.log: You sell what you worked out. Someone else takes the risk.
Some locks are better admired.

events.text: A forger in the Under-Cloud Market offers a new face in the Under-Cloud Market a sack of false Mid-Grade stones to pass at the Exchange.

ok.log: They pass. The Exchange is a little poorer.

fail.log: An Exchange clerk weighs one twice.

effects.log: You refuse. The forger shrugs.
The wardens thank you and watch you.

events.text: Someone has been reading the cranes' letters on the isle you work, and selling what is in them. The isle thinks it is you.

ok.log: You find them and leave them for the wardens.

fail.log: You find nobody, and the wardens find you asking.

effects.log: You lie low until it passes.

events.text: The Heavenly Calendar's festival crowds the bridges of the Jade Court so thickly that a sleeve brushes a sleeve every step. It is a thief's season.

ok.log: A good night. Your sleeves are heavy.

fail.log: A warden in festival robes catches your wrist.

effects.log: You enjoy it, like an honest immortal.

choices.text: Watch for other thieves and warn the crowd

effects.log: You warn three marks. They never know.

events.text: You come home to find your own pavilion robbed, neatly, by someone who left a single stone on your table as a calling card.

ok.log: You find them. They are good. You offer them work.

effects.log: You laugh. You deserved it.

events.text: A mask of white cloud-silk is offered to a new face in the Under-Cloud Market by a fence who pays in chipped stones: whoever wears it is remembered by no one.

effects.log: You buy it. Your jobs are easier, and lonelier.
You want to be remembered, a little.

events.text: A partner of yours in the Under-Cloud has been talking to the wardens. You see them coming out of a warden's pavilion at dawn.

effects.log: They break down. They were threatened. You forgive them, once.

ok.log: The wardens raid an empty treasury.

effects.log: You leave the isle that night.

events.text: A faction that ruined someone you loved below, before you ascended, keeps its treasury on an isle you know well.

ok.log: You empty it and give it to the poor isles. The faction never recovers.

effects.log: You let it go. It does not go quietly.

events.text: The Jade Court announces a pardon for thieves who return what they took, for one year only.

effects.log: You return one thing. Your notice falls.
You keep it all.

effects.log: You leave legends to the legends.

effects.log: You listen. The stories are better than your life.

choices.text: Leave the isle for a while

effects.log: You leave. The stories go on without you.

events.text: The job is too easy: a treasury with its ward open, a warden asleep, a chest unlocked.

effects.log: You walk away. Next morning the wardens are seen leaving the treasury, disappointed.

fail.log: The trap closes on your sleeve.

events.text: A letter climbs the white stairs: someone from your old life below has heard you are a great immortal now, and is proud.

choices.text: Send them a gift of stones

effects.log: You send stones down. They will never know where from.

fail.log: The faction catches you at the edge of the isle.

effects.log: You refuse. The elder understands, and is sad.

effects.log: The Court rules against the faction, slowly.

effects.log: The stones go through. The captain wants more next time.

ok.log: You fly them past at night.

effects.log: You decline. The captain finds someone else.

You send them home with a stone. They keep following you anyway.

effects.log: You send them stones every season.

ok.log: You get them out on a night with no wind.

effects.log: You stay away. It is safer.

effects.log: You find whose it was. They weep.

You refuse. The offer will not come twice.
You accept and warn everyone you catch.

effects.log: You enjoy it. The notice fades.

effects.log: You refuse. The forger shrugs.

effects.log: You lie low until it passes.

effects.log: You enjoy it, like an honest immortal.

effects.log: You leave the isle that night.

ok.log: You find them and leave them for the Court.

effects.log: You lie low.

ok.log: You empty it into the worlds it crushed.

effects.log: You let it go.

effects.log: You return one thing. The blot fades.

effects.log: You leave it.

ok.log: It goes cleanly. More faith arrives at dawn.

effects.log: You vanish into a mortal's dream for an age.
You refuse. You wake lighter.

events.text: The Eternal Arbiter's own clerk looks up from the Book of Fates as you pass, and keeps their finger on a line.

effects.log: You keep walking. You can feel the finger on your line all day.
They take it. The finger lifts.

ok.log: They smile. "Not yet yours," they say.

events.text: The King of the Unlit Sun weighs the faith you bring and offers half, because stolen faith tastes of where it came from.

effects.log: You take it.

ok.log: You get more.

effects.log: You keep it. It tastes of the world it was stolen from.

events.text: A young god of mischief wants to work with the legendary God Nobody Saw. They are very good and very loud.

effects.log: You work an age together. It is loud.
You refuse. They are caught in an age.
You teach them to be quiet. They owe you.

events.text: The faith you took last age was all a small god had. They are fading now, slowly, and do not know why.

effects.log: You give it back in secret. They grow solid again.
You keep it. You watch them fade.

choices.text: Find them a world to pray to them

ok.log: You find them a world. They will never know.

events.text: An old thief of the Unlit Sun tells you the rules: never from a world's only god, never during a famine, never a prayer for a child.

effects.log: You swear. Better jobs come to you.
You laugh. The old thief does not speak to you again.

choices.text: Ask where the rules came from

effects.log: From a god who broke all three, once.

events.text: The pantheons tell their young about The God Nobody Saw. Most of it is wrong.

effects.log: You listen. The stories are better than your life.

choices.text: Leave a sign to correct one

effects.log: You correct it. The young gods are thrilled.
You go quiet.

events.text: A domain's vault lies open, its god away, its seals asleep. It is too easy.

effects.log: You walk away. Next day the Court is seen leaving, disappointed.

ok.log: You take one thing and are gone.

events.text: A prayer rises from your old life below: someone you knew, now very old, thanks the gods for a good life and asks them to look after you, wherever you went.

effects.log: You answer in a dream. They laugh in their sleep.
You bless them with what you stole. It is the best use it was ever put to.
You let it pass.

events.text: Someone is stealing in your name across three domains, badly, and the Court thinks it is you.

ok.log: A young god who admires you. You teach them better.

choices.text: Do a perfect job and sign it

effects.log: Everyone can tell the difference.
They are caught. You are not.

events.text: One age you realise you have enough faith, enough stories, and that a god could simply stop.

effects.log: You stop. Your hands are quiet for the first time in ages.
One more. Gods say it too.
Never.

events.text: A small world begs the legendary God Nobody Saw to steal back its rain, taken by a pantheon's decree as a tithe.

ok.log: The rain goes home. The world sings.

fail.log: The pantheon seals you for it.

effects.log: You refuse. The world dries.
The Court rules, slowly, for the world.

events.text: A mortal king below offers a great deal of faith for the legendary God Nobody Saw to add ten years to his line in the Book of Fates.

ok.log: You write it. He lives ten more years, and is not a good king.

effects.log: You refuse. He dies on time.

choices.text: Write ten years for his kinder heir instead

effects.log: You write it for the heir. The kingdom is better.

events.text: A young god follows you through the Divine Exchange, watching your hands with worship. They want to learn.

choices.text: Teach them to keep a domain instead

effects.log: You teach them honest work.
They learn. The pantheons will hate you both.
They follow anyway.

events.text: A thief you know has been sealed under the Bell of Silence, and the small world that prayed to them has no one now.

effects.log: You look after it. It does not know the difference.

ok.log: The seal cracks. They are out.

fail.log: The Bell rings for you too.

effects.log: You stay away.

ok.log: You take it. The pantheon is shaken.

choices.text: Take it and give it to the world that prayed it

effects.log: The world that first prayed it has it back.
You decline. The King is amused.

effects.log: You accept. You are very good at it.
You refuse.
You accept and warn everyone you are sent for.

effects.log: You rest.

choices.text: Plan the theft of the age

effects.log: You plan it.

events.text: A warden of the Heavenly Prison walks the chain-bridges at dawn and stops at your cell, curious about the new face. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You answer politely. The warden comes back the next day to talk.
You stare. The warden smiles and walks on.

events.text: The only scroll you are allowed is the Heavenly Statutes, and you find in them a law nobody has read in ten thousand years. It is your first year here.

effects.log: It says a prisoner who mends a cell may leave a year early. You start mending.

events.text: An immortal in the next cell has been here since before the Jade Court was built. Nobody remembers what for, including them. It is your first year here.

choices.text: Ask them to try to remember

effects.log: They try for a year and remember a garden. That is all.
You leave it. They thank you for not asking.

events.text: A visitor is allowed to your cell: an immortal you barely know, who says they are only here because nobody else came. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You thank them. They come back every year.

choices.text: Ask them to carry a message

effects.log: They carry it, nervously.

events.text: The chain of cloud on your ankle thins in the noon light, so thin you can see through it. It is your first year here.

ok.log: It is thinner than it looks. You remember that.

fail.log: It is exactly as strong as it looks.

effects.log: You leave it. Patience is the only key here.

events.text: The Heavenly Prison feeds its prisoners dew and a single peach a year, and the peach is the best thing you have ever eaten. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You eat it over a whole day.

choices.text: Give it to the old prisoner

effects.log: They cry. They had forgotten peaches.

events.text: The block erupts: two fallen immortals have started a duel through the bars, and the chain-bridges are swinging. It is your first year here.

ok.log: You stop them. The wardens take note, kindly.

effects.log: You stay out of it.

events.text: A crane is allowed to bring you one letter. It is from your old life below, and they do not know you are in a cell above the clouds. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You write about the view. It is true, in a way.
You tell the truth. Their next letter is kinder than you deserve.

events.text: There is no roof on the Cloudless Cells, only the stars, closer than you have ever seen them. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You count them for a year and lose count.

choices.text: Name them for people you knew

effects.log: You name a star for everyone you knew below.

events.text: A rumour runs along the chains: the Jade Court will pardon a hundred prisoners at the turning of the Calendar. It is your first year here.

ok.log: Your name is on the list.

choices.text: Help the old prisoner petition instead

effects.log: You help them write it. They are pardoned.

effects.log: You trade. The art is real.
You keep your peach.

events.text: The wardens are arguing about which prisoner will break first. You hear your name. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You do not break. One warden pays another.
You pretend. A warden is kinder to you after.

events.text: Your sentence is nearly done. The cloud chain feels lighter every day, or you imagine it does. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You plan it in great detail. It will be a good day.
You make peace with it. You will miss the stars.

events.text: Following the old statute, you begin mending your cell: the frayed cloud, the loose chain. A warden watches, puzzled. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You mend it well. A year comes off your sentence.
You mend their chair. They are kinder after.

events.text: A great storm hits the Cloudless Cells. The chains sing, and the whole prison sways like a ship. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You hold on. It passes.

choices.text: Help the old prisoner hold on

effects.log: You hold them through the night.

events.text: A newly fallen immortal is chained in the cell beside you, weeping and furious. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You talk them through the first night. They will not forget it.
Everyone has a first night.

effects.log: You go deeper than you have in a century.
You meditate with one eye open.

events.text: A warden slips you an extra peach and a scroll that is not the Heavenly Statutes. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You thank them. They do it again next year.

effects.log: They tell you about it for a year. You can almost see it.
You promise. They do not believe you, and are grateful.

events.text: Sealed, you feel the worship of your worlds below thinning as they forget you. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You hold them. Some worlds keep praying.
You let them go, so they can pray to someone who can answer.

events.text: A pantheon offers to pay tribute for your release, in exchange for your service after. It is your first year here.

effects.log: They pay. You owe them now.
You refuse. You will serve your own time.

events.text: The Bell of Silence rings once, for a god somewhere else who is set free. The sound goes through you like wind. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You wish them well.
You count. One day it will ring for you.

effects.log: You tell them. They do not believe you.

ok.log: You push a little of yourself through. The mother lives.

fail.log: You cannot reach. You hear the prayer go quiet.

effects.log: You hold the prayer, unable to answer.

effects.log: You listen. It is strange to hear your life read.
You correct the clerk. They write it down.

effects.log: You hold it with your mind alone.
You let a little go to a neighbour. It is kinder.

effects.log: You send what you can through the seal.
You rest.

events.text: A young god is sealed beside you for a crime they will not name, and they are terrified of the silence. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You talk to them through the stone for a year.
They learn it.

events.text: Under the Bell you have nothing to do but be what you are, and you do it for an age. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You understand your domain better than ever.
You dream of the worlds below.

events.text: A clerk of the Court, reading your page aloud, skips a line, kindly. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You thank them. They skip it again next age.
They read it. It hurts, and is true.

ok.log: The seal breaks. You are out, and written in red.

fail.log: The Bell rings. Two more years.

effects.log: You decline. They try alone.

events.text: An ancient sealed god tells you, through the stone, what the first dawn looked like. It is your first year here.

effects.log: You listen for an age.

choices.text: Tell them about your first dawn above the clouds

effects.log: They have never heard of the Upper Realm.

events.text: Under the Bell of Silence there is no sound at all. You begin to hear your own domain instead, very faintly. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: You listen. You learn your domain better than in an age of ruling it.
You hum. The Bell does not allow it, and you stop.

events.text: A hairline crack runs across the seal over you. Light comes through it, from the gold sky. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: You watch the light move all day.

ok.log: It widens a little.

events.text: Your petition to the Heavenly Court has been read, the clerk says through the stone. It will be considered, in an age or two. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: You write another, shorter.
You wait. Gods are good at waiting.

events.text: A god sealed beside you speaks through the stone: they were a god of a sun that went out, and they have been here since. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: They tell you about it for a year. You can almost see it.
You promise. They do not believe you, and are grateful.

events.text: Sealed, you feel the worship of your worlds below thinning as they forget you. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: You hold them. Some worlds keep praying.
You let them go, so they can pray to someone who can answer.

events.text: A pantheon offers to pay tribute for your release, in exchange for your service after. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: They pay. You owe them now.
You refuse. You will serve your own time.

events.text: The Bell of Silence rings once, for a god somewhere else who is set free. The sound goes through you like wind. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: You wish them well.
You count. One day it will ring for you.

events.text: Sealed gods cannot be visited, but dreams can. Someone you love finds you in one. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: You tell them. They do not believe you.

choices.text: Ask them to look after your worlds

effects.log: They promise.

events.text: The oldest sealed god under the Bell says they no longer remember being anything else. A friend you made inside is listening too.

effects.log: You tell them what they were, from the Book. They weep.
You leave it.

events.text: A prayer gets through the seal somehow: a child below praying to you to make their mother well. A friend you made inside is listening too.

ok.log: You push a little of yourself through. The mother lives.

fail.log: You cannot reach. You hear the prayer go quiet.

effects.log: You hold the prayer, unable to answer.

effects.log: You listen. It is strange to hear your life read.

events.text: Your shape is carved on a jade warrant at every tollhouse on the cloud roads. The likeness is poor, which is the only good thing about it.

effects.log: You change everything about how you look.
You laugh. A warden hears you laugh.

events.text: The keeper of a wine house on a far isle recognises you from the warrant, and says nothing, and brings you a cup of tea on the house.

effects.log: You thank them. You never forget that cup.
You leave before dawn. They would have kept quiet.

events.text: A Jade Warrant hunter has your warrant and has followed you for three isles. Tonight they are waiting at your mooring.

ok.log: You win. They let your warrant drop, impressed.

fail.log: You lose, and wake in chains.

ok.log: You are gone.

events.text: Somewhere a warden has filed your warrant under a heavier one. The cloud roads feel a little wider.

effects.log: You rest.

choices.text: Do one more job while it is quiet

ok.log: It goes cleanly.

events.text: The wardens are watching every bridge of the isle you live on. You recognise three of them at the bazaar this morning.

effects.log: You stay home. The wardens get bored.

ok.log: They do not look twice.

fail.log: One of them looks three times.

events.text: A minister's steward suggests, very politely, that a gift to the Celestial Ministries might make the wardens look elsewhere.

effects.log: The wardens look elsewhere.
The wardens keep looking.

events.text: An old friend of the isles asks you, quietly, to stop visiting: the wardens are watching anyone who knows you.

effects.log: You stop. It is the right thing, and lonely.
You visit. They are glad, and afraid.

events.text: Your work in the Under-Cloud Market has made you a regular face below the isles, and the demons there have started calling you by a nickname.

effects.log: It means "the one who comes back." You like it.
They do not stop.

events.text: A demon of the Under-Cloud asks you to carry a jar to the Jade Court's own steps and leave it there. It is very heavy and very quiet.

effects.log: You carry it. Nothing happens. Yet.
You refuse. The demon finds someone else.

ok.log: It holds a petition from the Under-Cloud's poor. You carry it gladly.

events.text: A fallen immortal who owes the Under-Cloud a debt you were sent to collect begs you for one more year.

effects.log: You give it. Your employer is not pleased.
You collect.

events.text: The Heavenly Court has written your name in red in the Book of Fates. Every clerk who opens the Book sees it.

effects.log: You take another face for an age.

choices.text: Write a small line beside it

effects.log: You write something rude in the margin. A clerk laughs.

events.text: A small god's shrine on the edge of the sky takes you in, knowing what you are, because you once answered their world's prayer.

effects.log: You stay. They are good company.

choices.text: Leave before you bring the Court down on them

effects.log: You leave quietly.

events.text: A warrant-bearer of the Death Domain has been sent with the Court's writ. Tonight they find you.

ok.log: You win. They let the writ fall.
You are gone.

events.text: The ink of the red line beside your name is fading. The Court has other pages.

effects.log: You rest.

choices.text: One more theft while it fades

ok.log: It goes cleanly.

events.text: Clerks of the Court have been seen in your domain, reading the walls of your temples as if they were pages.

effects.log: You keep it quiet. The clerks get bored.

ok.log: They are flattered and go.

events.text: A judge's attendant suggests that tribute to the Heavenly Court might lighten the blot on your page.

effects.log: The blot lightens.
The blot stays.

events.text: One of your worlds has heard rumours of what you do, and its priests ask in prayer whether their god is a thief.

effects.log: You answer honestly. Some of them pray harder.

choices.text: Send a dream of a just god

effects.log: They are reassured.

events.text: Your quiet work for the Silent Hall has made you known in its corridors. Its lords nod to you now.

effects.log: You nod. You are one of them.
You pretend. They notice.

events.text: The Silent Hall asks you to carry a dream from one sleeping god to another and not read it.

effects.log: You carry it. Nothing happens. Yet.

ok.log: It is a love letter. You deliver it gladly.

fail.log: It is a curse, and it notices you.

events.text: A small god owes the Silent Hall a debt of forgetting, and you are sent to collect it.

effects.log: You let them keep one. The Hall is displeased.
You collect. They will not remember you.

events.text: You walk out of the Cloudless Cells onto a bridge of plain cloud, and the isles look exactly as they did. Nobody is waiting for you.

choices.text: Walk to the nearest wine house

effects.log: You sit down and order. The keeper does not ask.
You fly to a far isle and start again.

events.text: A faction steward turns your name away from a post: the Jade Court's records say you were held in the Heavenly Prison.

ok.log: They give you a chance.

effects.log: You accept it. Records are long above the clouds.

events.text: The friend you made in the Cloudless Cells is released too, and finds you at a mooring with nowhere to go.

effects.log: You take them in. They are the most loyal friend you have.
You give them a start and part as friends.

events.text: A minister is collecting accounts of the Heavenly Prison for a reform of the statutes, and has heard you were inside.

effects.log: Your account is read before the Court.
You keep it to yourself.

events.text: A warden tells you, off the record, that the Jade Court is considering casting you down the white stairs to the world below. For good.

effects.log: You lie low. The Court forgets to decide.

choices.text: Make a gift to the right minister

effects.log: The matter is dropped.
You laugh. The warden does not.

events.text: Long after you stopped, a young thief of the Under-Cloud finds you and asks if the stories are true.

choices.text: Tell them the truth, all of it

effects.log: You tell them. They leave thinking hard.

choices.text: Tell them it was someone else

effects.log: You lie. They do not believe you.

events.text: Something you stole long ago turns up for sale at the Isle Bazaar, at a price ten times what you got for it.

effects.log: You buy it back. You are not sure why.
You laugh. That is trade.

events.text: The child of the warden who has hunted you for a century gets lost on the cloud roads, and you are the one who finds them.

effects.log: You bring them home. The warden looks at you a long time, and stops hunting.
You leave them safe and go.

events.text: The Demon Realm offers you a place in its own courts, where thieves are lords. All you must do is go down and never come back up.

effects.log: You refuse. The clouds are your home.
You visit. It is very like the Jade Court, only honest about it.
You do one job for them.

events.text: One night above the clouds you cannot sleep, and count every immortal you have robbed. It takes until dawn.

effects.log: You repay one, in secret.
You sleep at last.

events.text: In the wardens' hall there is a jade slate with your outline on it, and no face. Wardens touch it for luck before a chase.

choices.text: Leave a face on it one night

effects.log: You draw a face. It is not yours. The wardens chase that face for a century.
You leave it. It is better as it is.

events.text: The Under-Cloud Market changes hands below the isles, and your old employers are gone. The new ones do not know you.

effects.log: You introduce yourself. Work comes.
You let it go. Your nights are your own.

events.text: The seal lifts and the Bell is silent behind you. The gold sky is very bright. Your worlds below have not noticed you were gone, mostly.

effects.log: You visit each of them in a dream.

choices.text: Rest a while in the light

effects.log: You rest.

events.text: A pantheon refuses you a seat at its council: your page in the Book says you were sealed.

ok.log: They give you a seat at the end.

effects.log: Pages are long among the gods.

events.text: The god you spoke with through the seal is freed too, and comes to you with no domain left.

effects.log: You share a corner of your domain. They are grateful forever.
You help them find a small, empty domain.

events.text: The Eternal Arbiter's clerk asks the sealed and the once-sealed about the Bell, for a reform of the sealings.

effects.log: Your account is heard.
You keep it.

events.text: A judge of the Heavenly Court lets it be known that a god who keeps stealing may be stripped of their domain.

effects.log: You go quiet.

choices.text: Pay tribute to the right judge

effects.log: The matter is dropped.
You laugh. The judge writes it down.

events.text: Ages after you stopped, a young god of mischief finds you and asks whether the stories about you are true.

effects.log: They leave thinking.
They do not believe you.

events.text: A measure of luck you stole ages ago turns up at the Star Market, sold by a god who stole it from you.

effects.log: You buy it back. It still has your fingerprints on it.
That is how luck works.

events.text: The youngest clerk of the Court, who has been reading your page for an age, is lost in a world below. You find them.

effects.log: You bring them back. Your page is read more gently after.
You leave them safe.

events.text: The King of the Unlit Sun offers you a dark shrine of your own, if you will never return to the light.

effects.log: You refuse.
You visit. The dark is very honest.

choices.text: Take one job for the King

effects.log: You take one.

events.text: A god does not sleep, but one age you rest and cannot, and count every god you have robbed.

effects.log: You repay one in secret.
You rest at last.

events.text: In the margin of the Book of Fates, beside a theft nobody can explain, a clerk has drawn a small picture of a god with no face. It is you.

effects.log: You add a smile. The clerks argue about it for an age.
You leave it.

events.text: The Silent Hall has a new lord, who does not know you.

effects.log: Work comes.
Your ages are your own.
